item.title: 49ers' ‘unc package' of Mike Evans, Keenan Allen catching passes, praise
item.description: Mike Evans (5) and Keenan Allen celebrate after Evans' touchdown reception against the Minnesota Vikings in the second quarter Sunday in Mexico City. (Agustin Cuevas/Getty Images) Mike Evans and Keenan Allen played 19 snaps together in the San Francisco 49ers ' 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. On seven of those plays, Evans and Allen were the lone wideouts in a two-receiver set. According to head coach Kyle Shanahan , that's called the "unc package." "We mix in so many guys, and I know everybody's name, but when I'm thinking about football and stuff, I don't always just spit out names fast," Shanahan said. "So sometimes it's just easier for me to say unc. Everyone knows who I'm talking about." What do Evans and Allen think about the nickname? "I hope they like it," Shanahan said. "I think it's cool. They're not, like, really uncles. They're in their 30s. They're still young." Evans, 33, and Allen, 34, are in their 13th and 14th NFL seasons, respectively. One is a 6-foot-5, 231-pound one-on-one matchup nightmare who can win over the top, up the sideline or across the middle of the field. The other is a smaller-but-still-big 6-2 receiver who thrives on short and intermediate routes. Despite having different builds, they bring a handful of shared qualities to San Francisco's offense, according to Shanahan. He couldn't stop listing them Wednesday. "They're still unbelievably talented" at their ages, he said, "but just the intelligence of both of them, and just the poise they have, and how competitive they are, and how good they are at whatever you ask them to do … just how good of blockers they are, how good they are at routes that you haven't seen them run before. "It's whatever you put in, they figure out." Did Shanahan have fun scheming them open Sunday? "Yeah, big time," he said. Evans caught six passes for 109 yards and a touchdown. Allen trailed with three catches for 38 yards. There were countless plays where they worked in unison. For instance: On Evans' touchdown catch late in the second quarter, Allen directly freed him up for a one-handed grab in the back corner of the end zone. Lined up together in a condensed formation - with the ball on Minnesota's 4 - Evans ran a corner route and Allen ran a zig underneath him. Three Vikings defenders were split between the two of them. Allen occupied a double team just long enough for Evans to win his one-on-one matchup against safety Harrison Smith. Once cornerback Byron Murphy Jr. recovered to chase Evans, it was too late. He was a step behind, and Evans was in for six. One quarter later, the 49ers were backed up on their own 5-yard line, and Brock Purdy needed to push the ball downfield against the Vikings' blitz-heavy defense. Minnesota sent six rushers at the quarterback, so the 49ers blocked seven. The only receivers running downfield were Evans and Allen. item.title: Hurricanes rally past Lightning in third, 3-1
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 22: Sean Walker #26 of the Carolina Hurricanes celebrates with teammates after scoring a goal during the second period against the New York Rangers at Madison Square Garden on November 22, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Jared Silber/NHLI via Getty Images) | NHLI via Getty Images The Carolina Hurricanes picked up their third win in a row and their 19th of the season with a gutsy road victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning by a 3-1 margin on the night before Thanksgiving. The Hurricanes got an exemplary performance from goaltender Brandon Bussi, who ultimately turned aside 32 of the 33 shots he faced and bought Carolina time to ultimately rally for the win in the third period. Bussi and Lightning goalie Andrei Vasilevskiy dueled to a scoreless first period before the Lightning built up a territorial advantage into the second period, when Anthony Cirelli struck just 55 seconds in on a power play goal on assists from former Hurricane Jake Guentzel and Nikita Kucherov. The Long Island native battled hard to keep the Canes down by just a goal for the duration of the second, as the Bolts mustered 7 high-danger chances in the frame. Carolina finally broke through offensively in the third period on an Eric Robinson tally when the speedy winger beat Vasilevskiy from a sharp angle after a flubbed puck and turnover by Tampa Bay defenseman Max Crozier. Just a minute and a half later, the Canes took the lead on a nice passing play when Jaccob Slavin got his first of the year by fooling Vasilevskiy into thinking a cross-ice pass was coming before depositing the puck into the suddenly-vacated portion of the goal. Sebastian Aho and Seth Jarvis picked up their 21st and 9th assists of the season on the play. Slavo shoots and he scores for the lead pic.twitter.com/fZPiJcBzLn — Carolina Hurricanes (@Canes) November 26, 2026 Carolina kept the Lightning from establishing dangerous possession in the zone as the clock wore down, and even had multiple bids to get an insurance goal at the empty net that were turned aside by some sharp impromptu goaltending from Bolts winger Brandon Hagel. Jackson Blake ultimately found the yawning cage to put the game away at 3-1. The win makes the Hurricanes the first team in the Eastern Conference to surpass the 40-point mark, but they did not extend their seven-point lead in the Metropolitan Division over the New Jersey Devils, who beat the Columbus Blue Jackets in a shootout. The Canes will be back in action again on Saturday when they host the Ottawa Senators.

item.title: Rams S Kam Kinchens ejected; Packers WR Christian Watson evaluated for concussion
item.description: (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images In the second quarter of the Green Bay Packers-Los Angeles Rams game, Rams safety Kam Kinchens was ejected for leaving his feet and leading with his helmet on a tackle attempt on Packers receiver Christian Watson. You can find video of the play below: Christian Watson gets CRUSHED and is down injured pic.twitter.com/U0etpi9e8G — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 26, 2026 Initially, a cart came out for Watson, but the receiver was able to leave the field under his own power. The Packers are currently listing Watson as questionable to return and say that he’s being evaluated for a concussion. To be honest, it looks like the biggest hit he ended up taking was when his head hit the turf on the way down, not necessarily Kinchens’ blow to Watson’s facemask. Green Bay was not awarded a first down on this play due to offsetting penalties. Packers receiver Matthew Golden was called for offensive pass interference (you can only set a pick within a yard of the line of scrimmage), so they simply replayed the fourth-and-one play. After not getting a man coverage look with their running back’s motion, like they had on the play that Watson was injured on, head coach Matt LaFleur called a timeout and elected to kick the football, setting up a 17-17 tie going into halftime. We’ll keep you updated when we hear more news on the Packers’ injury situation.

item.description: Tennessee quarterback George MacIntyre (12) on the field during a college football game between Tennessee and Texas A&M at Kyle Field in College Station on Nov. 14, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) NASHVILLE, Tenn. — Tennessee football enters Saturday’s rivalry matchup against Vanderbilt with an opportunity to strengthen its College Football Playoff position. The No. 7 Volunteers (9-2, 6-2 SEC) have emerged as one of the conference’s hottest teams. Meanwhile, Vanderbilt (4-7, 1-7) will look to spoil Tennessee’s postseason ambitions at FirstBank Stadium. Tennessee enters the matchup as a 13½-point favorite, creating expectations for another convincing performance. Here are three reasons the Volunteers could defeat Vanderbilt by more than two touchdowns. 1. Tennessee Is Playing Its Best Football at the Right Time Tennessee has built considerable momentum heading into the final weekend of the regular season. The Volunteers enter Saturday with nine victories and an opportunity to reach double-digit wins before the postseason begins. More importantly, Tennessee has demonstrated an ability to win physical SEC games while controlling the tempo. That approach should translate well against a Vanderbilt team that has struggled to consistently stop opposing offenses. The Commodores have allowed opponents to sustain drives, creating opportunities for Tennessee to establish its rushing attack. Additionally, Tennessee’s ability to control the football could gradually wear down Vanderbilt’s defense. If the Volunteers build an early lead, their physical running game could help turn a competitive matchup into a comfortable victory. 2. Jim Knowles’ Defense Creates a Significant Mismatch Tennessee defensive coordinator Jim Knowles has transformed the Volunteers into one of the nation’s strongest defensive units. The Volunteers enter the matchup ranked among the country’s leaders in defensive efficiency. Their ability to limit successful plays has made sustained scoring drives difficult for opponents. Meanwhile, Vanderbilt’s offense has struggled to consistently generate production against quality defenses. That creates a favorable matchup for Tennessee, particularly on early downs. Knowles’ defense can pressure opposing quarterbacks while limiting opportunities for explosive plays. Additionally, Tennessee’s defensive front should have opportunities to disrupt Vanderbilt’s rushing attack and force difficult third-down situations. The Volunteers also have an opportunity to correct one of last season’s biggest defensive failures. Vanderbilt rushed for 314 yards during its 45-24 victory in Knoxville last November. However, Tennessee enters this year’s matchup with a different defensive identity and a coordinator known for his aggressive approach. item.title: LeBron James hits triple-double milestone to power 76ers past Heat
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James hits triple-double milestone to power 76ers past Heat appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LeBron James has left Father Time dumbfounded again. The Philadelphia 76ers veteran forward willed his team to a big 111-104 victory over his former squad, the Miami Heat, on Wednesday at Xfinity Mobile Arena in the City of Brotherly Love. For the first time since he joined the 76ers, the 41-year-old LeBron James finished with a triple-double, scoring 25 points on 9-for-15 shooting from the field, grabbing 10 rebounds and dishing out 12 assists with a steal in 35 minutes of action. Making the four-time NBA Most Valuable Player’s night even more impressive is the fact that his latest triple-double was the 126th of his legendary career in the league. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “LeBron James just had his 126th career triple-double. That’s more than Larry Bird, Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant and Scottie Pippen COMBINED,” ESPN Insights shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter. James is about to turn 42 years old in December, but he showed that he can still carry a team to a victory. Without big man Joel Embiid and wi th Jaylen Brown unable to finish the contest , James became the biggest thorn in the side of Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat, even scoring 14 points in a row in the first half to give Philadelphia a 47-39 lead, while bringing the house down. Tyrese Maxey paced the 76ers in scoring with 30 points on 12-for-21 shooting from the floor, while VJ Edgecombe added 18 points for the home team. The Sixers improved to 15-4 overall and are now 2-1 in Group B play of the 2026 edition of the NBA Cup. item.title: Tom Brady Makes Strong Statement About 49ers QB Brock Purdy
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: Sports analyst Tom Brady looks on prior to the game between the Atlanta Falcons and the Chicago Bears at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers are coming off a massive win over the Minnesota Vikings last Sunday night. There was some concern heading into the game about how quarterback Brock Purdy and the offense would fare against Minnesota’s defense. However, Purdy quieted those doubts early, throwing three touchdown passes in the first half as San Francisco cruised to a 35-10 victory. On Wednesday, the NFL named Purdy NFC Offensive Player of the Week for the fourth time in his career. He also jumped Cincinnati Bengals QB Joe Burrow to become the slight favorite to win MVP entering Week 12, according to Kalshi. Tom Brady Makes Strong Statement on Purdy Now, ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Seattle Seahawks, FOX Sports announcer and NFL legend Tom Brady had some strong praise for Purdy. Brady will be on the call for the game and shared his weekly top 10 power rankings before the matchup. “He’s just operating a lot faster than everybody else,” Brady said of Purdy . “Some guys are operating at 1.0. Some guys are operating at 1.5. Brock’s operating at 2.0 right now. He’s thinking fast. He’s making fast decisions. The ball’s coming out of his hands quickly. You know when you listen to a podcast, and it’s at 1.0, but you speed it up to, like, 1.5 or 2.0? You just get so much more done.” The No. 1 spot in @TomBrady’s Power Rankings remains unchanged, but where did the rest of the teams land this week? https://t.co/O70DpDSKQV — FOX Sports (@FOXSports) November 25, 2026 Purdy has completed 71.0% of his passes for 2,564 yards, which ranks ninth in the NFL, and 23 touchdowns, which ranks third. He’s put up those numbers across 10 starts while leading the 49ers to a 9-1 record. Purdy Shows Up on Injury Report Some concern surfaced Wednesday when Purdy appeared on the injury report with an ankle issue he sustained in the second quarter against the Vikings. 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan revealed that Purdy would not practice Wednesday. However, he noted that the injury isn’t a high ankle sprain and considers the quarterback day-to-day. Purdy’s status over the next two days will be crucial in determining whether he can play Sunday. If he can’t go, backup Mac Jones would get the start. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Tom Brady Makes Strong Statement About 49ers QB Brock Purdy appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Chiefs Rule Out 3 Players in Final Injury Report Hours Before Pivotal Thanksgiving Showdown With Bills
item.description: Chiefs Bills Final Injury Report Getty The Kansas City Chiefs will be without three players when they face the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night, including starting running back Kenneth Walker III. The Chiefs released their final injury report on Wednesday, November 25, ruling out Walker, starting right tackle Jaylon Moore, and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott ahead of one of their biggest games of the season. However, Kansas City received encouraging news regarding starting right guard Trey Smith, who appears set to return after missing time with a concussion. The Chiefs enter the Thanksgiving matchup with an 8-2 record, trailing the 9-1 Bills in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed. Chiefs Rule Out Kenneth Walker III Despite Encouraging Practice Update Peter Woods and Noah Gray are questionable for our Thanksgiving matchup against the Bills. Kenneth Walker, Jaylon Moore, and Omar Norman-Lott are out. — Kansas City Chiefs (@Chiefs) November 25, 2026 According to the Chiefs’ official injury report , Walker will miss another game despite returning to practice on Tuesday. The running back injured his groin before Kansas City’s Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. He returned as a limited participant on Tuesday but did not receive clearance to play against Buffalo. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson has performed well in Walker’s absence and will once again have an opportunity to contribute against the Bills. Kansas City will also be without Moore, who has not practiced since suffering an ankle injury during the third quarter of the Chiefs’ Week 9 game against the New York Jets. Norman-Lott, meanwhile, remained a limited participant throughout the week as he continues working his way back from a knee injury. The Chiefs activated the second-year defensive tackle from the reserve/physically unable to perform list last week. Trey Smith Set to Return as 2 Players Remain Questionable Smith carries no injury designation heading into Thursday’s game after participating fully in practice again. The veteran right guard entered concussion protocol during the first quarter of Kansas City’s Week 10 matchup and has been working toward his return. Tight end Noah Gray received a questionable designation despite progressing to full participation in practice. Gray suffered a rib injury late in the Chiefs’ game against the Arizona Cardinals. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods is also questionable. Woods has not played since suffering a neck injury against the Denver Broncos in Week 8. item.title: ‘Prepared to throw it no times’: Joe Burrow ready to get extreme if he has to
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals Joe Burrow takes questions from media during a press conference after practice at Paycor Stadium, Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026, in downtown Cincinnati. The Cincinnati Bengals lost 22-20 to the Washington Commanders on Monday night in a game that many expected them to roll and pull away from the rest of the AFC North. The Bengals have been extremely pass-happy this season, and while it’s been largely beneficial, Monday’s loss highlighted the sort of issues that might surface down the stretch if the offense doesn’t find more balance. During his media availability on Wednesday, Burrow was asked if he felt the team needed to commit to the run more. It depends,” Burrow answered. “Obviously, you’d love to be super explosive in both. But we’ll play the game however we need to play to win it. And I’m certainly prepared for either one. I’m prepared to throw it no times. I’m prepared to throw it 70 times. Whatever it takes to win.” Joe Burrow when asked whether the Bengals need to run the ball more or more effectively over the rest of the season: “I’m prepared to throw it zero times. I’m prepared to throw it 70 times, whatever it takes to win.” #Bengals https://t.co/i6ahCl5vPx — Chatterbox Sports (@CBoxSports) November 25, 2026 After the Bengals scored in the third quarter, they only ran the ball twice more in the game. Running back Samaje Perine finished with only six carries for 26 yards and the team finished with just 36 yards rushing in total. Cincinnati is averaging just 79.4 rushing yards a game, third-fewest in the league this season. Cincinnati’s next game is against the New Orleans Saints, and Burrow knows that with the skill set of the Saints’ defense, his squad will have to adjust. “Their linebackers are good at blitzing,” Burrow said about New Orleans. “Their front is explosive, and they’re good rushers. When you put those two things in combination, it makes it hard. Just worried about trying to win this week. Landscape will play out the way it plays out, and we just got to keep winning.” If Cincinnati can’t run the ball against good defensive fronts, teams with good rushers like the Saints will be able to tee off on Burrow, and Cincinnati could find the momentum out of its sails fast. Burrow says he’s willing to do whatever it takes to win. Sunday’s game will be a great opportunity to see if he can prove that by following the gameplan. Casparius’ ceiling suggests he can still contribute at the MLB level in the future, but for now his focus will be on recovering from elbow surgery. Casparius made his big league debut in 2024 but only appeared in three games. He made a significant impact with 46 outings in 2025. However, he was limited to five outings this past season. It’s certainly an unfortunate blow, but it is worth mentioning that the MLB season could end up being shortened this year depending on how long it takes for MLB and the MLBPA to agree to a new collective bargaining agreement. Baseball fans are hopeful that the season will begin as scheduled in late March, but a lockout is expected to begin in early December at the very least. With the league and players’ association still far apart on the subject of a salary cap, there is no telling how long the expected lockout will last. In any case, Ben Casparius will work to recover and return for the 2028 season. Although he won’t pitch in 2027, it’s unclear exactly how many big league games he will miss given the uncertainty around the lockout situation. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Gotham FC’s home semifinal moved to 5K-seat stadium in field quality debacle
item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST “At this level, in this kind of game, as a league, and we should have a better surface,” Amorós said. “Unfortunately, our club and football club did absolutely everything in their power to make sure that was the case. Unfortunately, it wasn’t. But luckily, it looks like nobody got hurt, and the game was what it was.” It’s not immediately clear if the NWSL penalized Gotham for a second consecutive week because of the field. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. Getty Images The head coaching role will take on an even bigger role going into 2027 as NYCFC prepares for massive changes with the planned move into their new stadium and MLS changing their league calendar to a summer-through-spring format, which is in line with the European football calendar and includes an abbreviated sprint season that will run from February to May. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. NYCFC will begin its search for a new head coach immediately, sporting director Todd Dunivant said in a statement released late Sunday morning. “We would like to thank Pascal for his commitment and contributions to New York City FC and wish him and his family all the best. This decision follows a thorough review of the season and reflects our ambition as an organization,” he said. One of the biggest problems that NYCFC faced this season – especially during its struggles in the second half – had been allowing late goals that would cost the club points, or matches altogether. And the club dealt with a number of injuries during the course of the season, while also playing much of the year without one of its top scorers, Alonso Martinez, as he recovered from a torn ACL he suffered last fall. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
